entries.sense_en: made impossible; ruled out ahead of time

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb: decide something will not be considered or cannot happen.
synonyms.example: The doctor ruled out a broken bone.

synonyms.nuance: Stops an action from happening; preclude removes the possibility beforehand and is more formal.
Keeps a person or thing out of a group; less about making an outcome impossible.
synonyms.example: She was excluded from the list.

entries.sense_en: freedom from any punishment for what you do

synonyms.nuance: Legal or official protection from punishment or a duty; impunity is the fact of escaping it.
Formal permission not to follow a rule or pay a cost; not about avoiding revenge.
Informal, used with 'get off': escaping punishment or cost, often unfairly.

entries.sense_en: punishment given as payback for a wrong

synonyms.nuance: Personal, emotional payback; retribution sounds more formal and moral.
synonyms.example: He wanted revenge for the insult.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more literary than revenge; fierce and intense.
Neutral and general; may be fair or official, without the sense of payback.

entries.sense_en: get justice or payback for a wrong done to you

synonyms.nuance: Usually 'take revenge' or 'revenge oneself'; more openly personal and spiteful.
Hit back against an attack, often at once; no sense of justice.
Casual idiom: make someone suffer as you did.

entries.tip_ko: avenge는 억울한 일에 대한 정의로운 복수, revenge는 개인적 감정의 복수 느낌이 강합니다.

entries.sense_en: as I usually did; as was my habit

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday phrase with the same meaning.
Same meaning in ordinary English; wont is old-fashioned and literary.
synonyms.example: She walked, as was her habit.

synonyms.nuance: Formal adverb for what is normally done.

entries.modern: "as was my wont" → "as I usually did"

entries.sense_en: the act of killing someone or something as a sacrifice

synonyms.nuance: Common word for giving up or killing something for a purpose; immolation is formal and grim.
Killing in large numbers or brutally; no ritual meaning.
General ruin of something; not linked to sacrifice.

entries.sense_en: expert knowledge and taste, especially in wine or art

synonyms.nuance: Skill or knowledge in any field; connoisseurship stresses refined taste.
Personal sense of what is good; can be untrained.
Good judgement in telling quality apart; broader than wine or art.

entries.tip_ko: connoisseur는 프랑스어에서 온 말로, '카너서'처럼 끝음절에 강세를 두어 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: of a true connoisseur: loving and knowing fine art and rare things
entries.sense_ko: 진정한 감식가다운, 미술품·진귀한 것을 아끼고 알아보는

synonyms.nuance: Able to judge quality well; stresses judgement, not passion.
Having refined taste from education and experience.
Having skilled knowledge in any field; no sense of love for fine things.

entries.modern: "the true virtuoso spirit" → "the true connoisseur's spirit"
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 virtuoso는 주로 '거장, 명연주자'를 뜻하지만, 여기서는 '미술품·골동품 애호가, 감식가'라는 옛 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: pretending to be someone or something you are not, to cheat people

synonyms.nuance: Any crime of cheating for gain; not necessarily pretending to be someone.
General act of misleading; the most neutral term.
Something fake presented as real; refers to the thing, not the act.

entries.sense_en: a fake expert who pretends to have skill or knowledge

synonyms.nuance: Someone who falsely claims special skill to gain money or praise; more formal.
Informal and broad: anyone or anything not genuine.
Stresses deliberate cheating, not just lack of skill.

entries.tip_ko: 오리 울음소리 외에 '돌팔이 의사'라는 뜻이 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: felt proud of a skill or quality he had

synonyms.nuance: Talk about it proudly to others, often too much.
Feel pleased about it; more positive and quiet.
synonyms.example: She takes pride in her work.

synonyms.nuance: Informal and negative: showing off.

entries.sense_en: approached and spoke to me first, boldly

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: come near to someone, with or without speaking.
Say hello politely; accost may feel forward or unwelcome.
Call out to get someone's attention, often from a distance.
synonyms.example: He hailed a friend across the street.

entries.sense_en: the many-colored costume of a court jester

synonyms.nuance: Any clothes worn for a role or party; no color meaning.
Uniform of a servant or company, not a fool's dress.
Adjective for bright colors; motley also suggests a clash of mixed colors.

entries.sense_en: was topped by; had something placed on top

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word: be on top of, or cover the top of.
Sits on top like a crown; suggests something special or final.
Other sense of surmount: beat a difficulty, not physical position.

entries.sense_en: what is accepted as; what people call, though it may not be real

synonyms.nuance: Almost the same; often used with a person appearing to be something.
synonyms.example: He could pass as a local.

synonyms.nuance: Be mistaken for something else by accident.
synonyms.example: She was taken for her sister.

synonyms.nuance: Adjective showing doubt that the name is deserved.

entries.sense_en: a large wine cask holding about 126 gallons

synonyms.nuance: General word for a wooden barrel for wine or beer.
Everyday word for a round container; not tied to wine.
Small barrel, mostly for beer.

entries.sense_en: to what place; where to

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; 'where to' is needed to match whither's meaning of direction.
Modern spoken form for direction.

entries.sense_en: take unfair advantage of someone's kindness

synonyms.nuance: Bother someone a little; milder.
Formal: cause someone difficulty or extra effort.
synonyms.example: I don't want to inconvenience you.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and often negative: use someone for your gain.

entries.tip_ko: 이 대화에서는 상대의 호의에 폐를 끼친다는 정중한 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: troubled or made to suffer, especially by illness

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for having an illness or problem.
Troubled again and again over a long time.
Milder and more general than afflict.

entries.sense_en: covered with a hard outer layer

synonyms.nuance: Covered with a layer, hard or soft.
Covered thickly with something dried, like mud.
Almost the same; simpler word.

entries.sense_en: a white salty mineral that forms on damp walls
entries.sense_ko: 초석(젖은 벽에 생기는 흰 광물 결정)

synonyms.nuance: American spelling and the common name for the same mineral.
Plain description of any such crust.
synonyms.example: a mineral deposit on the wall

entries.sense_en: a grand town house in Italy

synonyms.nuance: Very large private house in any country.
Home of a king or ruler; palazzo can be a rich family's home.
Large country or seaside house.

entries.sense_en: took hold of; seized

synonyms.nuance: Grab quickly and firmly.
Plain everyday phrase.
synonyms.example: She took hold of the rope.

synonyms.nuance: Hold tightly with the hand; may be gentle or desperate.

entries.modern: "possessed himself of my arm" → "took hold of my arm"

entries.sense_en: left quickly and secretly

synonyms.nuance: Run away from danger; not necessarily secret.
Leave quietly without being noticed; lighter, no crime.
Get free from a place or control.

entries.sense_en: to celebrate and enjoy themselves noisily

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for marking an occasion.
Party wildly and noisily; more intense.
synonyms.example: The crowd reveled in the streets.

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and casual.

entries.sense_en: a holder fixed to a wall for a candle or torch

synonyms.nuance: Stands on a table or floor; sconce is on a wall.
Any wall support; not specifically for light.
Modern word for an electric sconce.
synonyms.example: a wall light in the hall

entries.sense_en: burning torches

synonyms.nuance: Common word; in British English also a flashlight.
Light inside a glass case; not open flame.
Wax stick with a wick; small light.

entries.tip_ko: 프랑스어에서 온 말로 복수형은 flambeaux이며, 영어에서는 끝을 [z]로 발음합니다(/ˈflæmboʊz/).

entries.sense_en: underground tunnels and rooms where the dead are buried

synonyms.nuance: One burial room, often under a church.
A single grave or burial building, above or below ground.
Arched underground room; may hold wine, money or the dead.

entries.sense_en: the way a person walks

synonyms.nuance: General word; also means a trip on foot.
synonyms.example: I know him by his walk.

synonyms.nuance: A long, confident step.
One movement of the foot; gait is the overall pattern.

entries.sense_en: eyes (a poetic word for round things)

synonyms.nuance: Ordinary word; orb is poetic and slightly strange.
The physical round part; sounds blunt or funny.
Scientific word for any ball shape.

entries.sense_en: watery liquid from the eyes or nose
entries.sense_ko: 눈이나 코에서 나오는 물 같은 분비물

synonyms.nuance: Slimy fluid from the nose or throat; the medical word.
Medical word for fluid coming from the body.
Clear liquid from crying; rheum is thicker, from drink or illness.

entries.sense_en: a drink taken in one go; a gulp of a liquid
entries.sense_ko: (한 번에 마시는) 한 모금, 한 잔

synonyms.nuance: One act of moving liquid down the throat; small.
Large, hasty mouthful.
synonyms.example: He drank it in one gulp.

synonyms.nuance: A small, slow taste.

entries.sense_en: an unpleasant sideways look showing bad or sly thoughts

synonyms.nuance: A smug smile; the mouth, not the eyes.
Angry, direct stare.
Stare in a rude, sexual way.

entries.sense_en: large barrels for wine or spirits

synonyms.nuance: General word for a barrel.
Everyday term; usually smaller than a puncheon.
Small barrel.

entries.sense_en: hidden inner parts of a place

synonyms.nuance: Where two walls meet; less deep or hidden.
The deepest part of something large.
Small nook set into a wall of a room.

entries.sense_en: was brave or rude enough (to do something)

synonyms.nuance: Have the courage to do something risky.
Do something risky, with some care.
Do something bold that maybe you have no right to do.

entries.sense_en: a large bottle or jug for wine

synonyms.nuance: Container with a handle and a lip for pouring.
Common word; narrow neck, usually no handle.
American word for a jug.

entries.sense_en: a lively movement of the hands or arms made to express something

synonyms.nuance: One clear movement with a meaning; gesticulation is bigger and more animated.
Movement with a planned message.
Moving the hand to and fro to greet or call.

entries.sense_en: strange and ugly in a way that seems unnatural or comic

synonyms.nuance: Very strange; not necessarily ugly.
Very ugly and horrifying.
Silly and ridiculous, often funny.

entries.sense_en: jumping back in surprise or fear

synonyms.nuance: A quick small jerk from fear or pain, without moving away.
Draw back slowly in fear or dislike.
Neutral action; no emotion implied.

entries.sense_en: an underground room used for burial

synonyms.nuance: Any grave or burial building above or below ground.
Arched room; may store wine or valuables.
Underground room for storage, not burial.

entries.sense_en: mixed together in a messy, random way

synonyms.nuance: By chance, with no plan.
Without care or order; slightly negative.
Without choosing or caring which.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 주로 '성적으로 문란하게'라는 뜻으로 쓰이니, 여기의 옛 뜻과 구별하세요.

entries.sense_en: look closely and with effort into something hidden

synonyms.nuance: Look hard at something hard to see; polite.
Look quickly, often in secret.
Look into other people's private things.

entries.sense_en: chained so he could not move

synonyms.nuance: Common word: hold with a chain.
Bind wrists or ankles with metal rings.
Use rope; casual.

entries.sense_en: extremely surprised or shocked

synonyms.nuance: Surprised, often pleasantly.
synonyms.example: I was amazed by the view.

synonyms.nuance: Shocked into silence or stillness.
Upset as well as surprised.
synonyms.example: He was shocked by the news.

entries.sense_en: beg someone strongly and emotionally

synonyms.nuance: Common word, sometimes desperate or humble.
Make an emotional appeal, often to be spared.
Push someone to act; less pleading.

entries.sense_en: said suddenly and loudly, in surprise

synonyms.nuance: Cry out from surprise or strong feeling; the normal word today.
Say something suddenly without thinking.
Shout something out loud.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 주로 '사정하다'라는 뜻이므로 '외치다'의 의미로는 exclaim을 쓰세요.

entries.sense_en: close an opening completely with a wall of stone

synonyms.nuance: Close tightly so nothing gets in or out.
Fill an opening; any material.
Close with bricks; near in meaning.

entries.sense_en: one layer or row of stones in a wall

synonyms.nuance: Any level lying on or under another.
Things in a line side by side.
Any height or step; general word.

entries.sense_en: listen carefully

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for hearing on purpose.
Pay attention and follow advice.
Listen secretly to others.

entries.sense_en: stubborn and unchanging; refusing to give way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; refusing to change your mind or action.
Continuing without stopping; often positive.
Wilful and hard to control.

entries.sense_en: feel about blindly in the dark (here, with his sword)

synonyms.nuance: Search clumsily, often for a small thing.
Plain phrase; no clumsiness implied.
synonyms.example: She felt around in the dark.

synonyms.nuance: Search deeply with a tool or finger.
synonyms.example: probe the hole with a stick

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 '성적으로 더듬다'라는 뜻으로도 쓰이니 주의하세요.

entries.sense_en: shouted loudly and continuously

synonyms.nuance: General word for speaking very loudly.
Loud, often angry or excited.
High and sharp, from fear or pain.

entries.sense_en: a small opening

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a space between things.
Long, narrow cut or opening.
General empty space in a surface.

entries.sense_en: a wall built for defense

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word.
Anything that blocks the way.
Strong wall or protection, also figurative.

entries.sense_en: Latin for "may he rest in peace"

synonyms.nuance: English form, often written R.I.P. on graves.
The usual Latin word order; Poe reverses it.
